reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The error-parser fallback truncates messages without a type at a numeric group; it should preserve the full original message and include a regression test.
1 open issue - [Preserve full message when stack-trace scanning truncates error text](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/1180#discussion_r4689578936) · New
What changed in this PR This PR addresses #1179 in the shared error parser used by both clients. It preserves the server error code when truncation removes the `(TYPE)` suffix. **Changes:** - Recognizes server-prefixed errors without a type as `ClickHouseError`, with `type: undefined`. - Adds unit tests for truncated messages and non-server error text. - Documents the behavior change in both client changelogs. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `packages/​client-web/​CHANGELOG.md` | Documents the fix for the web client. | | `packages/​client-node/​CHANGELOG.md` | Documents the fix for the Node.js client. | | `packages/​client-common/​src/​error/​error.ts` | Adds a fallback for server errors without a type group. | | `packages/​client-common/​__tests__/​unit/​error.test.ts` | Tests truncated errors and plain-error fallback. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: For `Code: 395. DB::Exception: boom (2), Stack trace (not a stack) ...`, this fallback returns only `boom (2)` because the earlier stack-trace scan cuts `head` at the numeric group, which is then rejected as a type. Slice the original `text` here so an error without a type keeps the full message, and add a regression test for this case.
